clue.text: Relevant staff brought in by Hollywood star (7)

indicators.note: something brought in by a person is taken inside, so the star's name holds the staff

blocks.note: Richard Gere, the film actor
to man a desk is to staff it

explanation.surface: Suitable crew hired by a big film name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' is the verb, to man; GERE takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both describe something that bears directly on the matter in hand.

clue.text: Father, swallowing alcoholic drink, recalled something peppery (7)

indicators.note: to swallow is to take inside, so father takes in the drink
recalled means called back, so the drink's letters run backwards

blocks.note: papa = father
kir, white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: Dad downing a strong drink and remembering something spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: Kir is a French aperitif of white wine and blackcurrant liqueur; only the drink turns round, not the father.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a red spice ground from dried sweet peppers.

clue.text: Move quickly, offloading first edition (5)

indicators.note: to offload is to get rid of, so the first letter is thrown off

blocks.note: to sprint is to run fast; its S is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A rush to unload the first copies off the presses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first edition' is a book term, but 'first' belongs to the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Publishing sense: a print run of a book makes up one edition.

clue.text: Source of American oil in USA, possibly (9)

definitions.text: Source of American oil in USA, possibly

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter
possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters

blocks.note: first letter of American
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A question of where America's oil comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: it describes the state and spells it.
explanation.definitionFit: An &lit: read straight, the clue names a major oil-producing US state.

clue.text: Intimate with rich, frolicking across a good summer? (13)

indicators.note: frolicking children run about in all directions, and so do these letters
across means spread over, so the rearranged letters go around the A

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A wealthy lover romping through a fine summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but one who sums; a good one is an arithmetician.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun on 'summer' as one who does sums: someone skilled at arithmetic.

clue.text: No opening to chomp chop (3)

indicators.note: a word with no opening has lost its first letter

blocks.note: to chomp is to chew noisily; its C is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A diner with no way in for a bite, told to cut things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chomp chop' sounds like a single phrase; the first is wordplay, the second the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, as with an axe: both mean to cut with heavy blows.

clue.text: Possession? Some get it legally (5)

indicators.note: some of something is only a part of it, so the answer is part of the words

blocks.note: the letters running across geT IT LEgally

explanation.surface: A legal question: how do you properly acquire ownership?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a stretch: the legal right to own something stands for the possession itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal sense: title is the right of ownership over property.

clue.text: Arrival time? ETA useless about end of cruise, on reflection (3,4)

indicators.note: about means around, so the dud goes around the E
the end of a word is its last letter
a reflection in a mirror is reversed, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: ETA as written
a dud is something useless
last letter of cruisE

explanation.surface: A cruise passenger's grumble that the estimated arrival was worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: ETA + D-E-UD reads back as DUE DATE; the question mark hints that the arrival is a baby's.
explanation.definitionFit: A pun on arrival: the day a baby is expected to be born.

clue.text: Women warm up what may be breakfast grain product (9)

blocks.note: W = women
to heat is to warm up
breakfast is one meal of the day

explanation.surface: Women heating up breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: The breakfast picture suggests porridge, but the answer is a flour.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a brown flour milled from wheat with some bran left in.
